answer: Weigh influence by escrowed coin, not headcount: every vote and payout scales with the balance an account locks on-ledger — like saffron by the gram, a mask mints no weight. A prism of masks splits one stake, but k heads holding B/k still sum to B; with per-head fees, splitting strictly loses. Weights stay linear — no square-root voting, no caps — or splitting regains its edge. The tally is carved in marble: anyone recounts the escrow. Coin costs linearly, so a wealthy farm still dominates; only free identities die.
